incremental_changes.summary: Replaced the combinational DEFAULT_NOREGS FPnew configuration with a distributed RV32FD pipeline. The wrapper now tracks its single outstanding FP transaction in active_q instead of feeding FPnew's combinational busy output back into the core fence/flush decision, removing the LUTLP-1 loop without changing interfaces.

incremental_changes.trigger: User-requested pipelined IROM/DATA RAM access without changing the SoC address map or peripheral contracts
incremental_changes.summary: Converted the CODE and DATA memory paths from request/wait serialization to strict in-order pipelining. The frontend now overlaps synchronous branch prediction with one 32-bit instruction request per cycle, tracks pending PC/prediction metadata with redirect epochs, the HXI crossbar uses per-master route and per-slave owner FIFOs, the generic FPGA memories accept one operation per cycle, DCache sends all four refill words independently of their responses, and the D-HXI wrapper tracks read/write response types in order. Timer, IRQ, APB, default-slave behavior and all address ranges remain unchanged.

pipeline_contract.response_order: strict request order; no transaction IDs
pipeline_contract.irom_steady_state_throughput: one 32-bit request/response per cycle when unstalled
pipeline_contract.data_ram_steady_state_throughput: one 32-bit read or write per cycle when unstalled
pipeline_contract.dcache_refill: four 32-bit beats issued in consecutive accepted cycles

incremental_changes.trigger: User-requested IPC optimization with frequency-preservation constraint
incremental_changes.summary: Completed the three prioritized performance changes: correct-prediction branches may continue issuing while branch-miss uops are blocked before scoreboard allocation; registered DCache load completion now bypasses into the load/store address-generation operand path; and load/store queue capacity was increased to reduce back-pressure. No new RAM-to-AGU asynchronous path or speculative backend flush path was introduced.

frequency_guard.note: The final branch-miss gating uses the current-cycle compare result because the existing recovery controller redirects frontend state but does not flush backend scoreboard state; a registered gate allowed wrong-path uops to pollute the scoreboard.

targeted_fixes: RSD reset is held for its cache/predictor RAM clearing sequence.
RV32M and FP32 execution RTL, FCSR/fflags and RT-Thread FP context handling are active.
Uncacheable DCache MSHR matching includes the 32-bit word offset, preventing MTIME_HI/MTIME_LO response aliasing without adding a full-address tag compare.
UART RX returns a character in the function return value, avoiding the old stack byte store/load window and reducing instructions.
The legacy one-event SocRV trace exports the RSD two-lane retirement count through order advances for non-intrusive IPC measurement.
Vivado portability fix changed the RAM bounds assertion from an unpacked-array comparison to ra[i] scalar comparison.

assumptions: Each HXI master permits up to eight strictly ordered CODE/DATA transactions; side-effecting slaves remain single-outstanding.
Two masters contending for the same HXI slave are serialized by per-slave round-robin arbitration.
Code and data memory are each 64 KiB.
Memory response latency parameters must be at least one cycle.
The RSD out-of-order core is the active CPU implementation; the superscalar and demo cores are not present in the active RTL tree.
The formal software and FPGA baseline is RV32IMF/ilp32f/O3 with single-precision floating point only.
